in_arabic.name: محفوظ
in_arabic.meaning: المحفوظ من الله، محفوظ من كل شر
in_arabic.long_meaning: المحفوظ هو من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني الحفظ من كل مكروه أو شر، وهو اسم يدل على الحماية الربانية، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وهم عندنا محفوظون'

in_urdu.name: محفوظ
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی حفاظت میں، ہر شر سے محفوظ
in_urdu.long_meaning: محفوظ کا مطلب ہے کہ اللہ کی طرف سے محفوظ کیا گیا، یہ نام اچھے معنی رکھتا ہے اور اسلامی روایات میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان

in_hindi.name: महफूज़
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की रक्षा में, हर बुराई से बचाया हुआ
in_hindi.long_meaning: महफूज़ नाम का अर्थ है कि अल्लाह की ओर से सुरक्षित किया गया है, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है और अच्छे अर्थों वाला है

in_pashto.meaning: د الله په حفاظت کې، له هر شر څخه محفوظ
in_pashto.long_meaning: محفوظ نوم معنی دا ده چې د الله له خوا څخه خوندي شوی دی، دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو سره سمون لري او په دیني لحاظ کې مهم ګڼل کیږي

in_english.name: Mahfoozh
in_english.meaning: Protected by God, saved from all evil
in_english.long_meaning: Mahfoozh originates from the Arabic root 'h-f-z', which means 'to protect' or 'to preserve'. This name is derived from the concept of divine protection and is mentioned in the Quran as one of the attributes of God. It signifies a person who is under the protection of Allah, safeguarded from harm and evil. Historically, it has been used in Islamic tradition to denote a sense of security and divine care. The name Mahfoozh conveys a sense of safety and spiritual security.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahfoozh" is deeply rooted in Islamic tradition and culture. The concept of being protected and safeguarded is an important one in the Islamic faith. This name evokes images of security, safety, and peace of mind, which are highly valued in any society, but especially so in Islamic culture. Moreover, the name may serve as a reminder to those who bear it to strive towards living a life that is free from harm, as a means of seeking God's pleasure and reward in the hereafter.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Mahfoozh" is multifold. On one level, it represents the belief that God (Allah) is the Ultimate Protector and Safeguarder of His creation. Thus, the person named Mahfoozh is seen as being under Allah's shield and care, and may feel a deep sense of surrender and reliance on God. On another level, the name can serve as a reminder of the importance of leading a virtuous and righteous life in order to seek Allah's protection and blessings in this world and the next. It can also inspire a sense of gratitude and thankfulness to Allah for His mercy and grace in shielding us from harm and misfortune. Overall, the name Mahfoozh can be seen as a powerful reminder of the divine protection and guidance that is available to all believers if they remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Chapter 10: The Reign of the Umayyad Caliphs - Al-Mahdi and Al-Mansur (661-750 AD) records that Al-Mansur bestowed the title 'Mahfoozh' (Protected) upon his son, who later became known as Al-Walid II.
historical_references.context: During his reign, Al-Mansur faced several rebellions and was keen on securing his succession. He granted the title Mahfoozh to his son to emphasize his protection and emphasize his role as the future caliph.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam's Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt) describes that during the rule of Al-Mansur's grandson, Hisham I, the troops were given the title 'Mahfoozh' as a reward for their loyalty and bravery during the conquest of Egypt.
historical_references.context: The title Mahfoozh meant that the soldiers were under the protection of the caliph and were assured of their rewards for their dedication and service.
